title: Ridged soft-dome fingertip with dual sensing and fail-safe slip warning
problem_restatement: Make a finger-scale touch fingertip from skin to hand controller that conforms, supports load, transduces stress, resolves location, warns slip, and transmits message.
mechanism_sentence: A soft ridged dome about 20 mm wide spreads even a 1 mN touch onto squeeze sensors for steady push and a vibration film for slip, and a tiny finger computer sends position, force and a fast slip warning to the hand.
decisive_choices: F1 molded Shore A 10 dome with ridges plus sipes (C3) because only it quantifies 1 mN to 0.470 mm spot at 5.78 kPa under 2.5 mm stack, beating clear pad needing optics and fluid skin that leaks.

F3 capacitive taxels plus vibration film (C18) because capacitive alone cannot carry 100 to 500 Hz vibration through 9.00 ms converter update, while split path keeps 0.269 pF base with 3.57 fF change plus volt-level slip signals.

F6 fail-safe heartbeat plus interrupt plus frame (C29) because frame alone at 51.2 kbit per s cannot meet 30.0 ms latency, while normally-held line drops to danger on wire break per track-circuit analogy.
open_question: Does the 30 ms slip warning loop close on built hardware under shake and grip load?
transfer_line: Pressure: ridged silicone dome -> gel interlayer -> capacitive taxel grid | Measured: on-finger converter and microcontroller filter -> hand controller

assumed_constraints.constraint: silicone-object friction mu 0.5 to 1.0 so 2 N grip holds without slip
soft stack above transduction stays under 2.5 mm so 1 mN pressure reaches films
flex tail needs at least 3.18 mm bend radius and dorsal routing clear of rim slip

concept.working_principle: Molded ridged dome spreads touch through gel to capacitive taxels for steady force and vibration film for slip on flat facets of a rigid core, static path via converter frames and dynamic path direct to microcontroller joined into fail-safe message with heartbeat plus slip interrupt plus full frame.

fabrication_steps.description: Print faceted rigid core with nail back plus M2 plus dovetail mount first, because skin, films and board all bolt to it.
fabrication_steps.method: 3D-printed rigid polymer core, 20 mm dia x 22 mm with M2 screw plus dovetail

fabrication_steps.description: Make capacitive grid on flat facets plus vibration film with flex tail next, because flat tiles must sit before soft drape covers them.
fabrication_steps.method: laminated polyimide flex with 1.5 mm electrodes, 200 um dielectric, 2.00 mm pitch plus 28 um film

fabrication_steps.description: Mold ridged dome with gel interlayer and bond plus clamp edge over core after, because thin stack must drape continuous skin over tiles.
fabrication_steps.method: molded Shore A 10 silicone dome, 20 mm dia x 22 mm, 1.5 to 2 mm skin under 2.5 mm stack, 0.4 mm pitch ridges 0.1 mm high

fabrication_steps.description: Mount on-finger board dorsally and join flex via ZIF plus cable to hand last, because electronics are tested after skin and flex are placed.
fabrication_steps.method: assembled PCB with converter plus microcontroller, 0.5 mm ZIF, 3.18 mm bend, 6-pin 5 V link

risks.mitigation: rub-cycle tear test plus primer peel check

risks.risk: flex tail breaks at mount under vibration
risks.mitigation: shake-plus-pull continuity test with dorsal routing

risks.risk: slip warning misses 30 ms window through slow frame
risks.mitigation: timed hardware loop test of direct vibration path

novelty_claim: Continuous ridged skin with micro-sipes draped like cornea over flat-faceted core plus split static-dynamic films joined by fail-safe heartbeat plus slip interrupt.

figure_spec.system_view: Fingertip section showing domed ridged skin over gel over vibration film over capacitive tiles on faceted core with flex to on-finger board and cable to hand

open_questions: Does the 30 ms slip warning loop close on built hardware under shake and grip load?
Does the micro-siped skin survive rub cycles without tear with primer bond intact?
Does the flex tail keep continuity across the mount under vibration plus pull?
